desc:
Cut the array nums of positive integers into consecutive non-empty blocks so that the sum of every block is at most cap. Return the number of different ways to do this, modulo 1,000,000,007. Two ways are different if they place a cut at different positions.

nums = [1,2,1], cap = 3  -> 3   (1|2|1, 1,2|1, 1|2,1; the whole array has sum 4)
nums = [5,1],   cap = 4  -> 0   (the element 5 can never fit)
nums = [1,1,1], cap = 9  -> 4   (any cut positions: 2^2 ways)
hints: Consider the last block of a prefix. For a prefix of length i, which starting points j give a legal last block nums[j..i-1]?
Let ways[i] be the number of cuttings of the first i elements, ways[0] = 1. Then ways[i] is the sum of ways[j] over all j < i with prefix[i] - prefix[j] ≤ cap. Adding them one by one is O(n2).
All numbers are positive, so the legal j form a contiguous range lo .. i-1 and lo never moves backwards when i grows. Keep the sum of ways[lo..i-1] in a sliding window.
editorial: With prefix sums pre, the block nums[j..i-1] has sum pre[i] - pre[j]. Then ways[i] = sum of ways[j] over all j < i such that this sum is at most cap. Because all values are positive, pre is strictly increasing, so the valid j are exactly lo .. i-1 for a start lo that only moves right as i increases.

Maintain S = ways[lo] + ... + ways[i-1] (modulo 1,000,000,007). When moving to i, add ways[i-1], then advance lo while the block is too heavy, subtracting ways[lo] as it leaves the window. Then ways[i] = S. This is the sliding-window prefix-sum optimisation of a DP, giving O(n) time and O(n) memory. If some single element exceeds cap the window becomes empty and the answer is 0.
solution:
def countCappedSplits(nums, cap):
    M = 1000000007
    n = len(nums)
    pre = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + x
    ways = [0] * (n + 1)
    ways[0] = 1
    S = 1
    lo = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        while lo < i and pre[i] - pre[lo] > cap:
            S -= ways[lo]
            lo += 1
        ways[i] = S % M
        S = (S + ways[i]) % M
    return ways[n]
